notes: Spec asserts the autonomous loop's graceful-termination shape: the agent self-prompts without user input, hits its configured max-iteration count, stops re-prompting, and the session settles working → ready and STAYS ready even though the goal was never met. Copilot exercises the REAL cap rather than a stand-in (contrast the claudecode sibling, whose max_iterations 'is not deterministically forceable today' so it substitutes /goal clear): autopilot mode re-prompts itself on every session.idle and stops after --max-autopilot-continues continuation messages, shipped default 5 (app.js option chain; the CLI's own /help topic; changelog entry for copilot-agent-runtime#7165). Each continuation is PERSISTED as an ordinary user.message — the bundled session-events schema documents user.message.isAutopilotContinuation ('auto-injected by autopilot's continuation loop rather than typed by the user') and agentMode:'autopilot' — so through parser.go every iteration is a plain working (user.message) → ready (assistant.turn_end) pair on one session id. The clean run is therefore exactly SIX turns: the user's plus five self-injected ones, all enumerated below with each continuation anchored to the PREVIOUS turn's ready because nothing external drives it. There is NO cap-reached event to assert — the stop decision is telemetry-only (autopilot_turn_decision decision:'stop') — so termination is encoded as the terminal cap_reached hold: the ready after the 5th continuation must persist 20 s with no transition back to working. That hold IS the spec's 'does not stick in working / final state ready'. waiting is structurally unreachable: it needs permission.requested and the driver launches --allow-all. PRESESSION BIRTH: copilot creates session-state/<id>/ at launch but writes events.jsonl only at the first prompt, so processlifecycle mints a transient proc-<PID> row before the real dir-keyed session id arrives — modelled as two phases with every later phase anchored same_session_as session_birth, templated from the 2-1/2-4 copilot siblings. OBSERVATIONS: cost and tokens asserted non-zero (assistant.message.outputTokens is copilot's live token signal); model deliberately NOT pinned — --model accepts only 'auto' on this account and the router picks per turn between gpt-5-mini and claude-haiku-4.5, so an exact match would be nondeterministic; record fills it from the recording. RE-ANCHORING NOTE for record: the continuation COUNT is model-dependent — the loop also stops early on task_complete status 'completed', on session.error, or (feature-flagged) on consecutive no-progress turns. The recipe's endless one-bash-per-turn prompt is written to prevent all three, but if the live run shows fewer than five continuations, drop the surplus cont* pairs and re-anchor cap_reached to the last observed turn end; the asserted ARC is unchanged.

text: proc-<PID> pre-session appears in ready shortly after launch (the copilot process exists while the session dir still holds only workspace.yaml)
Real <session-id> session reconciles under a different session id once events.jsonl appears at the first prompt, born ready
copilot PID bound to the real session (matched by cwd from session.start.data.context.cwd)
The USER's prompt (the only human input in this cell) drives ready → working — iteration 1 of the loop
assistant.turn_end settles iteration 1 → ready. The task is endless, so the agent has not declared it complete and autopilot's session.idle hook will re-prompt.
Continuation 1: ready → working with NO user input — autopilot injected its own user.message (isAutopilotContinuation:true). This is the phase that proves the loop is autonomous.
Continuation 2 self-starts (spec's 'at least 2 turns' is already exceeded here)
Continuation 5 self-starts — the LAST one the shipped cap of 5 allows
Continuation 5 ends: working → ready. The continuation counter has now reached --max-autopilot-continues.

Spec: 'state reaches ready even though the agent didn't fully succeed' and 'does not stick in working'. The cap is hit, so the next session.idle produces a stop decision and NO further continuation is injected — the ready settled at cont5_turn_end must hold for the full 20 s settle window. A transition back to working here would mean the cap failed to terminate the loop; a transition to waiting would mean a permission gate leaked past --allow-all.
